{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABepd5uA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhIKsG8", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 360, "title": "Unify Speaker and Speaker · streaming into one Speaker node with typed audio OR input", "body": "## Goal

**Expose only one `Speaker` output node in Graph Editor.** It should accept **either** completed synthesized audio or streaming audio on **one input**, expressed as a precise **union / OR type**:

```
Speaker.audio: SYNTHESIZED_AUDIO | AUDIO_STREAM
```

The user should simply choose **Speaker**, connect any supported TTS audio output, and have the correct playback behavior chosen automatically. No additional Speaker mode selector or extra user-facing explanation is needed.

## Current implementation

- [`extension/graph.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/graph.js) exposes two different palette types:
  - `SpeakerOutput` (label **Speaker**), input `audio: SYNTHESIZED_AUDIO`
  - `StreamingSpeakerOutput` (label **Speaker · streaming**), input `stream: AUDIO_STREAM`
- [`web/port-contracts.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/web/port-contracts.js) currently uses shared contract identities and `compatiblePorts(output, input)` checks. `ANY` accepts arbitrary inputs; **do not use `ANY` for Speaker**, as it would lose type safety. `ITEM` is an existing specialized union of text-like types, not audio.
- [`web/speaker-output.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/web/speaker-output.js) implements `SpeakerOutputNode` for complete clips and `StreamingSpeakerOutputNode` for ordered streaming events. Both have important but different buffering, underrun, event-boundary, cleanup, and Stop/Cancel semantics.
- [`extension/graph-runtime.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/graph-runtime.js) instantiates each Speaker separately. Session preparation also handles both types.
- Completed-audio producers: `Supertonic3` and `Kokoro` emit `SYNTHESIZED_AUDIO`. Streaming producers: `Qwen3TtsStreaming` and `CosyVoice3Streaming` emit `AUDIO_STREAM`.

## Required changes

### A. One visible Speaker with one OR-typed input

1. Remove **Speaker · streaming** as a separate Add Node item. Keep a single node displayed as **Speaker**.
2. Give that Speaker a **single audio input port** accepting exactly `SYNTHESIZED_AUDIO | AUDIO_STREAM` (a union input contract), not two visible input ports and not an unrestricted `ANY` port.
3. Implement/reuse an explicit composable **input-only union-contract mechanism** in shared port typing. `compatiblePorts()` should accept either concrete audio output and reject unrelated contracts (TEXT, NUMBER, ITEM, etc.). Preserve strict output contract identities and type-safe validation of saved graphs, editor wire previews and runtime Pipeline edges.
4. Keep **one incoming connection per input port**. “OR” means *either compatible type can connect*, **not** joining two edges simultaneously, automatically mixing streams, or silently converting streaming audio into completed clips.
5. Keep the UI simple: a single Speaker entry, one audio port, no mode switch, extra help paragraphs or redundant actions.

### B. Correct runtime dispatch and lifecycle

6. Implement Speaker playback that **dispatches according to the actual validated incoming audio kind** (or the statically connected source contract), not by guessing from arbitrary unvalidated properties. Validate each input's payload under the proper concrete contract. Do not allow a type mismatch to pass silently.
7. Preserve both existing playback behaviors:
   - `SYNTHESIZED_AUDIO`: queue completed clips and play them in order.
   - `AUDIO_STREAM`: honor start/chunk/end/abort boundaries and sequence IDs, ordered scheduling/sample-rate conversion, bounded buffering, and underrun/error reporting.
8. Retain appropriate overflow limits, Web Audio autoplay/user activation and **Enable speaker** behavior, Stop/drain, Cancel/immediate cleanup, context release and error reporting. Do not accidentally call the completed-audio handler on stream events or vice versa.
9. Do not share playback state between graph sessions or change global speaker output behavior; a single Speaker node is allowed to have only one connected input type for a given graph execution.

### C. Existing saved graphs and dependencies

10. **Preserve existing working graphs** that currently contain `SpeakerOutput` and `StreamingSpeakerOutput`. Normalize/migrate `StreamingSpeakerOutput.stream` connections to the unified Speaker's input where feasible on load/import, without changing graph wiring semantics; ensure export/save produces the canonical single-Speaker representation. Keep migration narrow and tested rather than maintaining two indefinitely visible/active Speaker implementations.
11. Check related subgraph boundaries, typed port checks, graph validation, snapshot/fan-out handling and generated graph examples for correct recognition of the new OR input.
12. Update docs/help/tests to describe one Speaker. Remove old separate Speaker references from Add Node and current examples without changing actual TTS generators or their output types.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Add Node → Outputs** shows exactly **one Speaker** and **no Speaker · streaming**.
- [ ] Speaker has exactly **one visible input port**; it accepts connections from completed TTS audio and streaming TTS audio outputs.
- [ ] The port rejects unrelated output contracts and enforces one incoming wire, both in editor and runtime validation.
- [ ] `Supertonic3/Kokoro → Speaker` plays completed audio normally.
- [ ] `Qwen3-TTS/CosyVoice3 → Speaker` plays audio incrementally with correct boundaries, order and streaming lifecycle.
- [ ] Switching between a completed-audio connection and a streaming-audio connection works after saving/reloading; no extra configuration/mode selection is needed.
- [ ] Existing saved graphs with either old Speaker node are migrated/kept usable without silent disconnections or playback regressions.
- [ ] Stop, Cancel, overflow, audio permission/activation, background/foreground, concurrent sessions and teardown retain existing safeguards.
- [ ] Test both valid audio types, invalid types, one-edge-only constraint, existing saved graph migration, and browser playback behavior; relevant tests pass.

## Suggested files

- `web/port-contracts.js`: narrow input-only union contract support, compatibility tests.
- `web/speaker-output.js`: unified dispatch and reuse of current completed/streaming playback.
- `extension/graph.js`, `extension/graph-runtime.js`, relevant session preparation: single Speaker node and runtime wiring.
- Graph Library import/normalization paths as needed to preserve old connections.
- Audio/speaker/graph-port tests and `docs/extension-graph.md`.

## Out of scope

- General-purpose type coercion, unrelated union conversions, implicit audio mixing, two simultaneous incoming edges, or changes to TTS model output contracts.
- More Speaker variants, configuration selectors, or explanatory UI.
